title: Ironclad Banking on-prem integration jot
content:
Customer: Ironclad Bank (mid-market retail + corporate banking)
Attendees:
  - Ironclad: Priya Rao (CTO), Marco Silva (Platform), Elena Cortez (Security/compliance), Thomas Y. (SRE)
  - Redwood: Maya (solutions), Kenji (infra), Lina (security review)
Call date/time: 2025-08-18 10:00 PT (notes captured 8/19/25)

High-level ask:
  - Host a private, VPC-isolated Redwood deployment in Ironclad's OCI tenancy (they prefer OCI but open to AWS if needed).
  - Low-latency inference for customer service assistant and KYC triage (p95 target ~ < 250ms for generation of short answers; embedding pipeline throughput ~ 50K embeddings/day).
  - Strict data controls: PII must never leave their VPC in plaintext, KMS with HSM-backed keys, audit logs retained for 7 years, SOC2 + PCI scope concerns.
  - Offline on-prem option for specific regulated flows (air-gapped staging for AML team).

Notes / tech constraints observed:
  - Network: corporate firewall with egress via proxy; no inbound from internet except for a management plane tunnel. They prefer a private control plane model (Redwood Private) that talks over a customer-initiated TLS tunnel / peered connectivity (VPN or OCI FastConnect).
  - Identity: internal SSO via Okta (OIDC). Need mapping for service accounts + per-team RBAC.
  - Storage: Sensitive transcripts must be encrypted at rest with customer KMS; backup snapshots may be retained in their object storage but need customer-managed keys and narrow ACLs.
  - HSM: Elena asked about FIPS 140-2 / 3 and HSM integration for signing and key usage. We need to confirm Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integration in OCI and options for key lifecycle policies.
  - Model variants: They asked whether we can run 7B quantized vs 13B and fallback to 70B on Dedicated (costly). For latency SLOs they prefer smaller quantized models. Kenji suggested redwood-base-7b-8bit for initial POC.
  - Quantization audit: Compliance wants to understand deterministic outputs when using quantized kernels (auditability). Need to document any slight nondeterminism and how we version/record model binaries + kernels.
  - Data residency: All inference and KV cache must stay in the tenancy region; cannot call hosted API for regulated flows.
  - Logging: Audit log retention 7 years requested—confirm retention pricing and storage mechanics. Also need atomic request logs mapped to conversation ids (for audit).
  - Network egress: They are sensitive to license/vendor egress to external repos; container image pulls must come from a vetted internal registry.

Performance & capacity rough numbers (customer stated):
  - Concurrent active sessions expected: 120 during peak.
  - Average tokens per request: 180 (generation + context).
  - Estimated monthly tokens: ~80M tokens/month.
  - Embeddings: 50K/day (~1.5M/month).
  - Desired p95 latency: <250ms for simple responses, <800ms acceptable for longer generative chains.

Architectural options we discussed:
  1) Redwood Private (VPC-hosted control plane + runtime in their OCI tenancy) with dedicated GPU pool (initially 2x A10G-equivalent nodes).
  2) Hybrid: Private control plane + Redwood Dedicated fallback (hosted) for burst capacity (BUT this may violate policy for regulated flows) — flagged as not allowed for PII flows.
  3) Air-gapped on-prem package for AML team (separate environment).

Key gotchas / risk areas to investigate:
  - Compliance: PCI/AML teams may require data to never transit outside on-prem. Need legal to confirm whether our support model (Redwood engineers accessing logs for debugging) is allowed; may need an escalation path where we ship runbooks and remote support is via customer-provided bastion only.
  - OCI specifics: We don't have exact experience with their OCI FastConnect flavour and private link naming. Kenji to confirm infra playbooks for OCI private deployments (images, SGs, subnet requirements).
  - Model licensing: check if any 3rd-party model license restrictions block on-prem edge deployment.
  - Determinism/QA: quantization may slightly change outputs — product needs to provide regressions/eval hooks (prompt tests) to show parity vs baseline.
  - Monitoring/tracing: need per-route token-level cost attribution in an air-gapped deployment (how will Console metrics be surfaced? local telemetry or push to their Splunk?).
  - Disaster recovery: RTO/RPO questions; they want failover across two OCI regions; we need to define geo-replication strategy for model artifacts and KV cache without leaking data between regions (legal to check).

Immediate action items (who -> what -> when):
  - Kenji: draft OCI network & infra checklist (subnets, SNAT/EIP, FastConnect/VPN choices, image registry), deliver by 2025-08-27.
  - Lina: produce security note on KMS/HSM integration + any FIPS/HSM compliance gaps, deliver by 2025-08-25.
  - Maya: prepare POC scope and cost sketch (2-node GPU pool + storage + 3-month run), include token cost estimate and embedding pipeline cost, deliver by 2025-08-28.
  - Sales/AE: ask Ironclad to complete Security Questionnaire and provide SOC2/PCI artifacts (ownership: Marco), target 1-week.
  - Schedule: architecture deep-dive workshop with Ironclad infra + security on 2025-08-26 (proposed).

Open questions for customer:
  - Can platform team accept our collector agent connecting outbound to Redwood control plane, or must we operate the entire control plane in their tenancy?
  - Clarify exact retention policy required for logs (7 years stated; are there different classes and retention access levels?).
  - Do they require on-prem support SLAs (we need to propose a support model if no remote access allowed)?
  - Which registry will host our runtime images? Do they allow ECR/OCI registries with signed images?

Stuff to include in follow-up pack:
  - One-pager: Redwood Private for regulated banking (network diagram + compliance notes).
  - Cost sketch: 3-month POC + steady-state 12-month estimate + optional air-gapped add-on cost.
  - Checklist: Security questionnaire answers, infra checklist, runbook for incident debugging without direct access.
  - Mini-eval: prompt regressions showing quantized 7B vs float outputs for their critical prompt set.

Notes-to-self / negotiation bits:
  - Be conservative on promised latency for quantized models — instead promise SLO for platform + show POC numbers.
  - Try to push them to allow a limited managed fallback for non-PII flows — that unlocks cost savings during bursts.
  - Prep a redlined support engagement that includes a vetted on-call engineer shipped in-country if air-gapped ops needed (costly but acceptable for enterprise).

Next meeting: proposed architecture deep-dive 2025-08-26 09:00 PT.

Quick links / refs I want to attach:
  - internal: redwood-private-deploy-playbook (CONFLUENCE-PRIV-305)
  - infra cheat: oci-fastconnect-notes (CONFLUENCE-OCI-12)
  - sample cost calculator: https://internal.redwood/cost-calc/poc-samples

End of jot.
